title: Heterogeneous Layerwise KV Quantization Sweep and Fidelity Analysis
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: evaluate heterogeneous (per-layer and per-key) quantization and lightweight compression schemes for the KV cache to reduce GPU memory footprint while preserving generation quality across continuous batching workloads. Hypothesis: selective per-layer FP8/INT8/INT4 encoding combined with chunked dequantization and short-prefix full-precision pins can reduce KV memory by 40-70% with <3% relative degradation on automated metrics and <5% human preference loss on long-context prompts. We will also measure stability under continuous batching (mixed prefix lengths) and observe variance/catastrophic failure modes at low precision under heavy batching.
acceptance_criteria: Memory reduction goal: >=40% KV footprint drop for 70B-style activations under default serving batch distribution
Quality: <=3% relative increase in model perplexity on heldout LM test set and <=5% embedding drift for retrieval embeddings compared to baseline fp16 cache
Stability: no >0.5% incidence of catastrophic token degeneration in top-k sampling tests (n=50k samples) when deployed with continuous batching enabled
Operational: quantized cache path must not increase p50 token latency by >5ms on p4d-like instances during production-like batching profiles
experiment_plan: Sweep axes: per-layer dtype {fp16,fp8,int8,int4}, per-head vs per-kv chunking, chunk-size {64,128,256}, delta-quantization vs linear quantization, and prefix-pin thresholds {0,32,128 tokens}
Benchmark suites: lm-perplexity (WikiText+OpenWeb), generation coherence (LLM-Eval subset), embedding drift (MS MARCO subset), sampled-degeneration tests (top-k/top-p distributions)
Workloads: three continuous-batching traces — low-latency chat (short prefixes), long-context doc-completion (prefixes >2048), and mixed PLG traffic (real production trace sampled from staging)
Infrastructure: run experiments on dedicated 8xA100-80GB machines, simulate service-level batching with our runtime harness (trace replay), record per-token latencies and GPU memory allocations
Measurement: automated metric collection + small human A/B (n=300 prompt pairs) on top candidate configs, log PRNG seeds and sampling parameters to reproduce degenerate cases
Safety-net: implement a runtime hot-revert that re-expands quantized KV to fp16 on detection of high-entropy divergence or score collapse (staleness-aware recompute)
Deliverables: bench results dashboard, candidate config JSONs for runtime, a short runbook for phased rollout
results_summary: Baseline: fp16 KV cache for 70B-lm activations consumes ~31.2GB per shard under our trace
INT8 global: reduced KV to ~19.8GB (-36%), perplexity +1.9% on LM test, embedding cosine drift 1.5%, negligible latency change (+2ms p50)
FP8 per-layer hybrid (heads 0..n-6 kept FP8, last 6 layers INT8): KV ~13.6GB (-56%), perplexity +2.8%, small increase in top-k tail entropy leading to 0.9% sampled-degeneration cases

INT4 aggressive: KV ~9.0GB (-71%), perplexity +7.2% and embedding drift 6.8% — unacceptable for retrieval and structured-output workloads, but viable for cache shards of cold prefixes if recompute fallback available
Chunked dequantization (256B chunks) reduces CPU/GPU memcpy overhead vs whole-buffer decode by ~18% and halves spike latency in batched decode scenarios

Continuous batching effect: low-precision encodings (INT4/INT8) amplify variance when batch contains mixed prefix lengths — observed 2.3x higher variance in next-token probability mass on mixed traces vs homogeneous short-prefix traces

Human A/B (n=300) across mixed long-context prompts: FP8-hybrid chosen 89/300 less often than fp16 baseline (relative loss ~6.1%), INT8 global chosen 34/300 less often (relative loss ~11.3%) — preference concentrated on factuality and long-range coherence cases
decisions: Primary recommended config: per-layer hybrid FP8/INT8 with last 4 layers kept FP16 for highest-fidelity tasks (tradeoff: ~50% KV reduction, expected ~3% perplexity delta).
Fallback policy: runtime detects high-entropy divergence or prefix-staleness and transparently re-expands relevant KV segments to fp16 for the affected request (graceful degrade).
Rollout gating: start with non-customer-facing internal tier and Dedicated customers on test clusters, then enable for hosted API with opt-in flag for best-effort low-cost tier.
Disable INT4 for now: reserved for offline archival cache only; do not enable in production without further mitigation and extended human evals.
next_steps: Implement dynamic precision selector in runtime: choose per-request quant profile based on prefix length and model variant
Add low-latency chunked dequantization path to runtime C++ kernel (PR in progress)
Run longer tail-safety sweep on 1M sampled tokens with adversarial prefixes to validate fallback heuristics
Prepare rollout docs and console flags: cost-estimates, KPI dashboards, and incident playbook
